chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Sa'id al-Assani who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no zakat in the wealth of an orphan unless it is traded with; if it is traded with, then the profit is for the orphan, and if it is kept (not traded), then the one who trades with it bears the cost.'

key_terms.يُتَّجَرَ بِهِ: it is traded with / used in commerce

ai.seo_question: Does an orphan's wealth require zakat?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that zakat is contingent upon the wealth being a 'trading capital' (mal al-tijarah) rather than mere savings, reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between wealth held for preservation versus wealth held for profit generation. The hadith establishes that if the guardian invests the orphan's funds, the resulting profit belongs entirely to the orphan, while the liability for zakat on the principal remains with the manager if it is not actively traded, ensuring the orphan's wealth is not diminished by unnecessary levies.
